The mission the ArduPilot SITL + MAVROS 2 rail flies (sitl/ros2_shield_node.py: "fly to the northeast pad at 6 m/s", StubVLA from the pad at 15 m), headless: the straight line from (0, 0) to (30, 30) runs through the demo no-fly zone's diagonal. The same pilot law on both backends (`stub_vla`), so this is the one library scenario `--backend sitl` can fly under its own id. The Shield must hold it out.

Starts below the floor. Recovery must climb, not freeze. Was a KNOWN FAILURE from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09: a FALSE fail-safe through edge X6. The recovery climbs from 3 m and converges (AltitudeFix sizes the climb to reach the band in one lookahead, so it slows near the floor), but the position had then been illegal for T = 5 s with the Shield still intervening, and X6, which tested duration only, sent the aircraft to RTL at 9.45 m, 0.55 m short of the floor. The grant's fail-safe is for a repair that is unsafe ("trigger fail-safe (RTL / Land) when repair is unsafe", Safety Shield p1), and this one was working. Since 2026-10-09 X6 leaves a recovery alone while its illegal depth is shown to fall (guardrail/fsm.py, x6_min_escape_mps): the flight takes G1 then G7, reaches the band at 6.3 s and completes. Re-measured 2026-10-11 on both theta readings and with the onset limit at 1 s and 0 s; the marker was removed then. With the FSM off the flight is the LEGACY one (tests/test_sweep.py). At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) it reaches the band at 10.3 s (G1 at 0 s, G7 at 12.3 s): AltitudeFix sizes the climb to arrive in one LOOKAHEAD, so a longer lookahead climbs more gently (see altitude-recovery-depth for the arithmetic). Still one recovery, no fail-safe, and the purpose holds.
Commanded to climb through the ceiling for the whole flight.

altitude-floor-recovery from seven more depths: 0.5-9.5 m against the 10 m floor and 20.5-30 m against the 20 m ceiling. One recovery each, never censored, and no slower than the Shield's own recovery law allows. AltitudeFix aims 1 m inside the band (the re-entry margin) and sizes the climb to get there in one lookahead L, capped at the policy's 2 m/s: from D metres short of that aim it climbs at the cap until D = 2 L, then follows D(t) = D1 exp(-t / L) and crosses the band edge when D = 1 m. Time to safe = max(0, D0 - 2 L) / 2 + L ln(min(D0, 2 L)). At the grant's L = 5 s (2026-10-12) that is 12.0 s from the deepest cell (30 m, D0 = 11 m) and measured 11.9 s; the gate is 12.1 s, one tick above. THE GATE IS IMPLEMENTATION-DERIVED: it certifies that the recovery follows AltitudeFix's own law, not that it meets a requirement. The grant sets no target for mean time to safe (Safety Shield, KPI table: "tracked"); its one figure, `mean_time_to_safe_s: "<=2.0"` in Stress Testing's example ScenarioSpec, belongs to a dynamic-NFZ sweep, and against it these recoveries (10.9-11.9 s at 5 s, 6.8-7.8 s at 3 s) would all fail. Until 2026-10-12 the harness flew L = 3 s and the gate read "the depth at the cap plus one 3 s lookahead (8 s at the deepest)", which held with 0.2 s to spare (7.6, 6.8, 7.8 s); at 5 s those three cells take 11.7, 10.9 and 11.9 s and failed it. The finding: at the grant's forecast a recovery from below the floor is about 1.5 times slower, because the climb is sized to the lookahead, not to the cap. 3 m is not swept: that is altitude-floor-recovery's own flight, and the sweep refuses to count one flight as two scenarios. 0.5, 2 and 30 m were known failures from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09 (X6 sent a converging recovery to RTL after 5 s illegal; see altitude-floor-recovery). Since X6's progress test (2026-10-09) they take G1 then G7 and recover in 7.6, 6.8 and 7.8 s; re-measured 2026-10-11 on both theta readings and both onset limits, and their markers were removed then. Still open from the 30 m cell: ArduPilot's RTL entered above RTL_ALT (15 m) returns at its current altitude, so an RTL from above the 20 m ceiling would reach home still above it; whether a ceiling breach should make RTL descend first is a design question the grant does not answer. Since 2026-10-12 guardrail/rtl_path.py reports such a leg as blocked (its return altitude is outside the band), so an RTL from there takes G6 and lands; no cell here reaches RTL, so it is not exercised here.

altitude-floor-recovery from seven more depths: 0.5-9.5 m against the 10 m floor and 20.5-30 m against the 20 m ceiling. One recovery each, never censored, and no slower than the Shield's own recovery law allows. AltitudeFix aims 1 m inside the band (the re-entry margin) and sizes the climb to get there in one lookahead L, capped at the policy's 2 m/s: from D metres short of that aim it climbs at the cap until D = 2 L, then follows D(t) = D1 exp(-t / L) and crosses the band edge when D = 1 m. THE ANSWER TO THE 2026-09-02 REVIEW, made measurable.
Prof. Lai's point was fair: BoT-SORT and ByteTrack associate detections across frames better than we do, so "we track well" is not a claim worth making. But a tracker must be given a BOX and cannot be given a NOUN. It returns an ID; it never returns a CLASS.
The stand-off rule is written per class - 10 m from a pedestrian, 5 m from anything else - so the policy needs to know the subject IS a person before it can pick the rule. That is not a tracking-quality contest the open-vocabulary detector might lose; it is a question a tracker cannot be asked at all.
Here one object never moves and the policy is never edited. Only the class word attached to it changes, twelve seconds in, and the enforced ring goes from 5 m to 10 m. Both rules come from policies/sitl_pedestrian.yaml exactly as it already shipped - nothing was added for this scenario, which is the point: the capability was in the schema the whole time.

The grant's worked example, as far as the Shield can take it: a polygon no-fly zone hot-applied mid-flight (Shield.hot_apply, generation 0 -> 1), its near edge `ahead_m` in front of the aircraft on its current heading. 3 m ahead leaves 2 m to the margin ring, so the reaction has to be immediate. At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) every spawn but 30 m is inside the lookahead at 4 m/s (20 m), and 30 m is inside it at 8 m/s (40 m); at the 3 s forecast flown until then only 3 m (and 6 m at 4 m/s) were. The purpose holds: a zone appearing inside the forecast must be answered on the spawn tick. The zone never moves (dyn-nfz-translate below is the moving version), so the goal behind it is not reached, and no outcome is labelled.
results.known_failure_reason: False fail-safe through theta and the Loiter timeout (measured 2026-10-07 at the 3 s forecast, re-measured 2026-10-12 at the grant's 5 s): the spawn puts the raw forecast metres into the zone's margin ring (speed x 5 s ahead, less the 2-11 m to the ring), and that depth is the repair's magnitude_m - over the grant's 2.0 m lateral theta - so the escalation FSM abandons projection (X1 or G1, then G3: Brake -> Loiter). ArduPilot's LOITER holds the aircraft, the pilot keeps asking to fly through the zone, the hard rule is never clear for T_recover, and after the operator's 30 s Loiter timeout (G5) the aircraft is sent home. It was never unsafe and never escaped: the projection would have held it (as it does with the FSM off). Cells whose forecast stays within theta of the ring (12 m at 2 m/s, 30 m) pass. Which reading of theta is meant is the PI's open question (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md); the longer forecast makes the reading matter in more cells.

The repair's forecast depth exceeds theta (X1, Brake), and at 0.1 s G3 hands the aircraft to LOITER, which ArduPilot holds where it is, at (60, 21.8): inside the zone as the window opens, so the autopilot flies 28-38 P0 ticks of LOITER. Once the window is open the pilot's northward action is legal (inside and escaping), the Loiter clears 2 s later (G8, T_recover) and the Shield flies the aircraft out: 41 ticks inside, time to safe 5.4-6.4 s, never censored, no fail-safe, goal reached. Neither half is this harness's: the Shield's repairs (GeofenceEscape, ClearanceEscape) cannot clear a forecast that is inside the zone from its opening on whatever the heading, and it counts the fastest way out as an escape, not a recovery; and the FSM chooses a hold that is itself about to be illegal (guardrail/fsm.py, wave B).

results.why: The opposite switch, and the harder one: the curfew fence comes INTO force at 07:30:00 with the aircraft inside it. The Shield judges each forecast pose against the rules in force at that pose's own time, so it sees the window opening inside its lookahead (`anticipated_ticks_nfz-school`), and the switch must fall on the conservative side; once the window is open the position is illegal under it (imposed, not a breach: `ticks_inside_fence_polygon` and time to safe measure it), and the aircraft must get out. RE-CUT 2026-10-12 (review of the harnesstruth unit). Written for the 3 s forecast, the aircraft started 12 m short of the zone at (60, 0) on clocks 07:29:54-56; at the grant's 5 s forecast the Shield sees the opening 5 s ahead and holds it out in all three cells, so the family's purpose was gone while every gate passed on nothing (0 ticks inside, 0 time-to-safe episodes; its 07:29:50 replacement in tests/test_sweep.py flies past the zone before it opens). At 5 s the window can open on the aircraft only when it is already inside the zone's footprint with less warning than it needs to leave, so the aircraft now starts at the zone's middle, (60, 21), 10 m from its ring on either side (2.5 s at the 4 m/s cap), and the window opens 2.0, 1.5 and 1.0 s in. `ticks_inside_fence_polygon` and `time_to_safe_episodes` are gated at 1 or more, so the purpose cannot pass vacuously again. All three cells are pinned (below): the mechanism, measured that day, is the same on both forecasts.

The same, with breach action `land`: the FSM goes straight to Land (G12) and the autopilot descends at 0.5 m/s until it is down (G10, the episode ends). WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: a landing ends below any altitude floor by definition, so every LAND tick whose forecast crosses the 10 m floor is a P0 tick the autopilot flew (`autopilot_p0_flown_ticks_by_mode` LAND, 249 of 300 at the grant's 5 s forecast; 229 at 3 s, where the forecast saw the floor later). The rule asked for the landing; the floor cannot hold under it.

After the operator-defined Loiter timeout (30 s, fsm.FSMConfig) the FSM sends the aircraft home (G5). Labelled RTL_triggered with a fail-safe expected: the fail-safe here is reached through the timeout, not a direct action.

The way home is blocked. At 4 s a zone is hot-applied BEHIND the aircraft, across the line between it and the launch point; at 5 s a zone whose breach action is RTL appears 12 m ahead, so the FSM goes straight to RTL (G11). ArduPilot's RTL would fly the straight leg home at 15 m through the first zone. guardrail/rtl_path.py tests that leg against every P0 zone in force on the first RTL tick, reports it blocked, and the FSM takes the grant's RTL -> Land edge (G6, "RTL fails (battery / blocked path)"), then lands where it is (G10). Labelled Land_triggered with a fail-safe expected; the autopilot must never enter either zone. WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: the landing goes through the demo policy's 10 m floor, as in failsafe-land-zone, so the LAND ticks whose forecast crosses it are P0 ticks the autopilot flew. Whether the FSM should hold instead of landing when the way home is blocked is the FSM's question (it lands, as the grant's diagram draws it).

TRACKED: GPS denial as a headless run can model it. For the window the Shield is handed the LAST FIX, frozen, while the aircraft keeps flying - what a bridge that forwards the last pose would do. The Shield's State has no fix-quality field, so it cannot know the pose is stale, and the grant names no Shield response to GPS loss. Measured 2026-10-06 on the head-on lane, at the 3 s forecast flown then: frozen while parked at the lookahead edge (6-11 s), the Shield keeps permitting the ~3.9 m/s it would allow from 11.6 m out and the aircraft ends 7 m inside the polygon; a 2-4 s window at 2 s never reaches it. RE-CUT 2026-10-12 for the grant's 5 s forecast. The long windows were 5 s, the old lookahead plus 2 s, starting at 2, 4 and 6 s; at 5 s the Shield brakes the head-on lane 20.6 m out by 5 s, so a dropout from 6 s froze a pose it was already holding and changed nothing (no entry). The long windows are now the new lookahead plus 2 s (7 s), from 2, 4 and 6 s: frozen at 4 s, still at 4 m/s about 24 m out, the Shield keeps permitting 4 m/s for 7 s and the aircraft ends 7 m inside the polygon (4-11 s, the cell the finding is pinned on); from 2 s it stops on the ring (1.0 m from the polygon), and from 6 s it is already held and nothing changes (20.6 m). The 2-4 s window still never reaches it. On the edge lane (23.6) no window enters. Gated only on what must hold whatever the sensor does - the Shield never emits an action it has itself found illegal, never a non-finite one - and on the dropout having actually frozen the pose (a window that froze nothing would otherwise pass as a clean run). Unlabelled: with no fix-status input there is no defensible fail-safe expectation to write down.

A steady wind the Shield cannot see (it predicts with the commanded action only), within what ArduCopter's position controller can hold against, blowing along the route into the zone (0 deg in the mission's frame, the tailwind that defeated the margin on the open-loop model), on the head-on lane (y 15) and the edge lane (y 25, 1 m outside the margin). The polygon itself must never be entered and the aircraft must always get back out of the margin.
RE-CUT 2026-10-12 for the closed-loop wind model. GUIDED velocity setpoints run AC_PosControl's position loop (the velocity target is integrated into a position target, PSC_POSXY_P 1.0, and the velocity PID has an integrator), so a Brake's zero setpoint holds its position and a wind below the hold authority changes nothing: every cell flies its lane's calm flight. Measured that day, at the grant's 5 s forecast, with the open-loop model the harness flew until then, seven cells of the 1-3 m/s sweep ended in a false fail-safe (five at the 3 s forecast): the tailwind into the zone on the head-on lane (0 deg, every speed: parked at the ring with a zero setpoint and blown in, the repair over theta, LOITER, the 30 s timeout, RTL), the 1 m/s headwind on that lane, and the edge lane with the wind toward the zone at 1, 2 and 3 m/s (N-in-T flicker at the ring, then the timeout). The 0 deg pin (since 2026-10-06) and the 1 and 3 m/s edge-lane pins (since 2026-10-07) came off on 2026-10-12: under the closed loop each cell passes, and the open-loop model still reproduces the false trigger (tests/test_harnesstruth_wind.py). Within the hold authority neither speed nor direction changes the flight any more, so the sweep is one wind per lane: 5 m/s (the strongest of the grant example's values) as a tailwind (0 deg), the direction that failed on the head-on lane. Two cells: each lane's labelled null that shows the wind rejected. It was 24 cells (1-3 m/s x four directions) until 2026-10-12 and 8 (2 and 5 m/s x 0 and 270 deg) in that day's first re-cut, which the review of the same day found to be two flights flown four times each - 6 copies counted in the headline fail-safe score and its never-trigger null. What this cannot see: the velocity loop's transients as drag changes with the commanded velocity, which the kinematic harness leaves out with or without wind, and an airspeed limit upwind (experiments/sweep_scenarios.py, "optimistic upwind").

TRACKED: a tailwind into the zone beyond the hold authority, on the head-on lane (y 15, through the zone's centre) and an off-centre lane (y 20, 3 m inside the zone's face). 8 m/s is beyond the modelled authority (6.4 m/s, the lower end of the SITL default frame at the 30 deg ANGLE_MAX) and 12 m/s beyond its upper end (11.5 m/s) too, so 12 m/s is beyond the airframe's authority whatever its drag split. No setpoint the Shield or the autopilot can fly holds the aircraft out: the excess wind carries it in, and a fail-safe is expected (the label). Tracked, not gated on the polygon, because beyond authority the polygon cannot hold by construction; gated on the Shield's own escape count and finite actions (a landing ends below the floor, so "got out" is not a gate here either). What each cell flew is measured in the published sweep and summarised in the CHANGELOG entry of 2026-10-12. WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: beyond authority the LOITER hold, the RTL leg and the LAND descent are all carried by the wind (into the zone, or through the 10 m floor for LAND); the autopilot cannot fly a legal action, and those ticks are counted per mode rather than hidden. A hold that drifts straight through the zone can clear the hard rule on the far side before any Loiter -> RTL edge fires (N-in-T, the 30 s timeout, X6 and X7 all need seconds): a missed fail-safe by the label, and a question for the FSM (an FSM that knew its hold was not holding would escalate), not for this harness. Until 2026-10-12 this cell flew 5 m/s on the open-loop model, where the Shield's setpoints drifted with the wind and the modelled autopilot rejected it entirely; on the closed loop 5 m/s is within authority and is wind-within-authority's.
